links.outcome: Flesch Reading Ease readability of ChatGPT responses to Helicobacter pylori questions
links.effect: ChatGPT-4 had the highest Flesch Reading Ease score, 24.88 (SD 0.44), which is very difficult to read; no significant readability differences among versions.
links.quote: In terms of readability, ChatGPT-4 achieved the highest Flesch Reading Ease score of 24.88 (standard deviation 0.44), however, no statistically significant differences in readability were observed among the versions.

links.outcome: Repeatability of responses when each question was submitted three times over three days
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o was most accurate (mean 4.46, SD 0.82) but had relatively low repeatability; ChatGPT-3.5 was most stable but occasionally gave incorrect answers.
links.quote: Despite its high accuracy, ChatGPT-4o exhibited relatively low repeatability.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the accuracy, reliability, and readability of three versions of ChatGPT (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4o) on clinical questions regarding Helicobacter pylori infection, but does not evaluate a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
